uncited: It differs from the underlying [Sobel Gradient Magnitude Approximation](1429-sobel-gradient-magnitude-approximation.md) by adding a lookup-based mapping and the final multiplication step, rather than just computing the raw magnitude value.
Each entry specifies a point on a piece-wise linear function.
**Compute Squared Magnitude**: Calculate the sum of the squares of the gradient components $(g_x, g_y, g_z)$.
**Map to Lookup Index**: Map the magnitude $M$ into the range $[0, 255]$ using the piece-wise linear function defined by GmLUT.
Since GmLUT has 8 entries at equal intervals, the input domain $[0, 2^{20}]$ is divided into 7 segments.
